sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Two-way if-else statements help your program make decisions between two options. It's like choosing between two doors - only one path gets taken!

• How to write if-else statements
• When to use two-way decisions
• How to handle yes/no situations in code

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're at a traffic light. If it's green, you go. If it's red, you stop. That's exactly how if-else works!

Two-way if-else statements let your program choose between two actions based on a condition:

• If the condition is true → do the first action
• If the condition is false → do the second action

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Always has one condition and two possible outcomes
✓ Only one branch executes - never both!
✓ The else part is optional but handles the 'false' case
✓ Braces {} are optional for single statements but recommended

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Test both true and false cases
donts: Don't forget the else part when you need it
Don't nest too many if-else statements
Don't use = instead of == in conditions
Don't put semicolons after if/else conditions
sections.protip: Use meaningful condition names like 'isAdult' instead of 'x > 18'

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Two-Way if-else Statements used in real apps?

examples.how: Check if username/password is correct (valid login) or not (show error)
Check if item is in stock (show 'Add to Cart') or out of stock (show 'Notify Me')
Check if player has enough points (level up) or not (keep playing)

problem.description: Write a program that checks if a number is even or odd. Ask the user to input a number and print 'Even' or 'Odd' using if-else.
hints: Use the modulus operator % to check remainder
A number is even if number % 2 == 0
problem.explanation: The modulus operator % gives the remainder after division. If a number divided by 2 has no remainder (== 0), it's even. Otherwise, it's odd.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Two-way if-else makes decisions between two options
📌 Always has one condition and two possible outcomes
📌 Practice with simple yes/no scenarios first
📌 Ready to learn about nested if-else next!
